historical_references.reference: Sharvikaariyan were a group of Hindu merchants and traders who flourished during the late medieval period in the Deccan region of India. They were particularly active in the trade of textiles, horses, and precious stones.

The Sharvikaariyan were also known for their religious patronage, particularly towards the god Shiva. They built several temples and funded the maintenance of existing ones. One of their most famous temples is the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi, which is a major pilgrimage site for Hindus today.
